heading: Outside, and ready for winter.
lede: Siding, trim, porches, and shutters. We wash first, scrape and prime what needs it, and watch the weather before we start.
includesHeading: The whole outside of the house.
includes: Siding — wood, fiber cement, aluminum, and stucco
Caulking open joints before they let water in

faq.question: When is exterior painting season?
faq.answer: Roughly April through October here, depending on the year. Paint needs the temperature and the damp to cooperate, so late fall through early spring is usually a no. Call anyway and we will tell you honestly whether it is worth waiting.

faq.question: What happens if it rains partway through?
faq.answer: We stop, and we cover what needs covering. Exterior work is planned around the forecast, so a wet week can push the finish date. We will keep you told rather than leaving you guessing.

faq.question: Do you pressure wash?
faq.answer: We wash, and how hard depends on the siding. Old wood and soft stucco can be damaged by too much pressure, so the setting matters more than the machine.

faq.question: How long will it last?
faq.answer: That depends on which side of the house, how much sun and weather it takes, and what is under the old paint. A sheltered north wall and a south wall that bakes all afternoon are two different jobs. We will tell you what we are seeing when we come look.

steps.title: Wash it
steps.body: Dirt, chalk, and mildew come off first. Paint does not stick to a dirty wall, and no amount of good paint fixes that.

steps.title: Scrape and sand
steps.body: Loose and peeling paint comes off, and hard edges get feathered so you cannot see the old line through the new coat.

steps.title: Prime and caulk
steps.body: Every bare spot gets primer. Open joints get caulk. This is the part that decides how long the job lasts, and it is the part nobody sees.

steps.title: Paint, watching the sky
steps.body: Two coats, working with the shade rather than against it. We do not start a wall we cannot finish before the dew or the rain.

stepsLede: Exterior work lives or dies on what happens before the paint. Washing, scraping and priming are most of the days on site, and they are the reason one job lasts and another starts peeling.
